newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: British mercenary leader leaves PNG.
newsitem.headline: British mercenary leader leaves PNG.

text.p: Mercenary leader Tim Spicer, who led 70 African soldiers on an aborted mission to Papua New Guinea, has left the South Pacific nation, a spokesman for the British High Commission said on Wednesday.
The retired British colonel had been detained in Port Moresby for the past month, but flew out of PNG for Sydney on Tuesday afternoon.
"He left at 3.00 pm (0500 GMT) yesterday, but we do not know his future plans from Sydney," the spokesman told Reuters.
Spicer, who was freed to leave PNG on Tuesday after a court dropped illegal firearm charges against him, said he was keen to return home to London.
His 70 African soldiers had already been thrown out of the country by army officers who rebelled against the mercenary deal and forced prime minister Sir Julius Cahn to step aside.
